findings.title: 47.8% of blocked verdicts carry a class word VERDICT_CLASSES lacks; bus.sh and fixer.md teach a second vocabulary
findings.claim: Over the 569 merged pull requests first-parent in v7.1.0..92d38ecb, 214 of the 448 parseable blocked verdicts (0.478; 93 distinct words, on 155 PRs) carry a class word that web-fix-wave.js's VERDICT_CLASSES does not hold, so parseVerdict routes every one to `other` and no bucket can be read off the grammar for them; 71 of them (ci-red 63, ci-cancelled 4, ci-pending 2, red-unanswered 1, body 1) are words that bus.sh's MECHANICAL_CLASSES and fixer.md's 'Never for a mechanical-only gap' paragraph teach, 9 of bus.sh's 12 mechanical words being absent from VERDICT_CLASSES.
findings.mechanism: Two writers of the block vocabulary and one reader: VERDICT_CLASSES (web-fix-wave.js, read by policy_lint.mjs:blockClasses and the wave's parseVerdict) and MECHANICAL_CLASSES (tools/audit/seat/bus.sh:672, taught by dev/governance/roles/fixer.md:311), while fix-review.md teaches the class as free `[a-z-]+`. check-wave-script.mjs's taught-word check reads only `blocked <sha> <word>:` examples in briefs, so fixer.md's prose list and bus.sh's shell variable never meet it. The same verdict is therefore `mechanical` to bus.sh dispatch and `other` to the wave and the --stats class table; 143 further verdicts are untaught by both (bus.sh's 'an unknown one refuses').

findings.proposed_fix_scope: One block vocabulary: VERDICT_CLASSES carries bus.sh's mechanical words (or bus.sh derives MECHANICAL_CLASSES from it), fix-review.md's class teaches that list rather than any [a-z-]+, and check-wave-script.mjs's taught-word check reads fixer.md's mechanical list and bus.sh's variable

findings.title: 60.3% of accepted ## Friction entries name no policy file; the body contract never resolves the rule id
findings.claim: Of the 174 `## Friction` entries policy_lint.mjs:frictionEntries accepts in the bodies of the 569 merged pull requests first-parent in v7.1.0..92d38ecb, 105 (0.603; 84 distinct ids) name no `--budgets` path under D13.M6's rule and 0 are ambiguous, so only 69 (0.397) attribute friction to a policy file, because checkPrBody refuses only an entry's shape and never that its `<rule_id>` names a rule.
findings.mechanism: The template asks for `<rule_id>: <event>: <evidence>`; frictionEntries accepts any FRICTION_ID ([A-Za-z.][A-Za-z0-9_.#/-]*) and checkPrBody (policy_lint.mjs:7317) refuses only an entry whose id is null. Ids such as `brief` (4), `handoff-wip`, `frugal-routing`, `PROMPT.md`, `fixer-step-push` (3 each), `r10-process-slim-1..5`, tool and group names pass the contract and key their own verbatim histogram rows, so friction a seat aimed at a contract section (fixer-step-push, fixer-brief, fixer-step-6: 6 entries) reaches no policy file under either keying, and checkSunset's honour-rule test reads only the file keys.
